description: Discover the historic train station in AR
longDescription: The train station was a central hub for the development of St. Georgen. Use AR To learn how rail transport shaped the region.
quizQuestion: What made the station historically important?
arStartDescription: Tap Start to allow motion and gyroscope access and load the AR view.
arStartErrorFallback: Failed to start the AR view.
tourFrontText: You are looking at the front of the historic Schwarzwaldbahn steam locomotive. Notice the powerful boiler and the classic front lamp assembly.
tourBackText: Now you are behind the train. Here you can see the tender area where coal and water were stored to keep the locomotive running.
tourInsideText: You are now in the driver's position. This is where the engineer controlled steam pressure, speed, and braking during the journey.
tourDriveHint: Look around and move your phone to see out the windows.

frontLamp.title: Front Lamp
frontLamp.text: The front lamp identified the train at night and illuminated the track ahead. Early lamps burned oil or carbide – electric lighting came only much later.

smokestack.title: Smokestack
smokestack.text: Smoke from the firebox escaped through the smokestack. Wide spark-arrester caps protected the surrounding forests from fire – especially important in the Black Forest region.

boiler.title: Steam Boiler
boiler.text: Coal fire heated water inside the boiler to over 180 °C. The resulting high-pressure steam drove the pistons that turned the wheels – the true heart of every steam locomotive.

tender.title: Tender
tender.text: The tender was the locomotive's rolling supply tank. It carried up to 8 tons of coal and thousands of litres of water consumed continuously during each journey.

rearBuffers.title: Buffers
rearBuffers.text: Spring buffers absorbed shocks when coupling wagons and during braking. Every locomotive had two buffers at each end to protect both engine and carriages from damage.

pressureGauge.title: Steam Pressure Gauge
pressureGauge.text: The pressure gauge showed the engineer the live boiler pressure. Optimal operating pressure was around 12–14 bar. If it rose too high, steam had to be released – otherwise an explosion was risk.

throttle.title: Regulator Valve
throttle.text: The regulator opened or closed the steam inlet valve to the cylinders. More steam meant more power and speed – precise, experienced hands were essential for smooth control.

brake.title: Brake Lever
brake.text: Brake control was especially critical on the winding Black Forest Railway. Braking too late on a steep downgrade could make the train uncontrollable – every move had to be exact.
